note: One door per job. Every host in the estate is declared here and nowhere else: the edge proxy is rendered from this file (christ/deploy/Caddyfile, checked by christ/test/domains.test.js), so a domain that is not listed is a domain that does not answer.

mail.about: telno.services is the sending domain: every notice, verification code, invoice and report leaves with this From, so its SPF, DKIM and DMARC records are the ones that decide whether mail lands.

hosts.about: The company: what the product is, what it costs, and the signup that buys it. Also the address every message is sent from. The root opens on the sign-in; the marketing page moved to /welcome.
Self-serve: a plan, a card and a working extension without talking to anybody.
The phone in a pocket: the browser softphone and the native app.
Numbers as records: the registry, the lookup and what a DID is worth.
Handsets and handsets' provisioning: sign-in, the softphone, and the /<vendor>/<mac>.cfg a desk phone fetches on boot. This is also the SIP domain.
The worldwide phonebook. The root redirects into the directory itself rather than a landing page that would sit in front of it.
The estate itself: every layer of the system and whether it is up, served by the CHRIST board.
The CHRIST board under its own name: the front door to the estate, what is running and whether it is up.

AgentOps: the Capstone Control Center — the agent definitions, the workflow studio, the dashboards and the supervision that keeps dograh answering, over cantus-control and cantus-ari. It gets its own origin because the console is a single-page app: its assets, its /api aggregator and its /ws softphone socket all live at the root, and a page served under another product's prefix loads blank.
The name the old PBX's admin page answered on. FreePBX and AvantFax went with Asterisk; the console is the administration surface now, so this name reaches it rather than a dead port.
The voice app's own name: dograh's UI, which was published on the retired box and is published here.
The other PBX name, same job as pbx.innotel.us: the panel, not the phone system.
The third PBX name, kept answering so a bookmark outlives the box it was made on.
The fax portal, which never moved off this stack: sending and receiving still run on the same switch.
The workflow studio. Its editor lived on the retired box's edge and lives here now; the container itself was always this stack's.
The document store the grading workflow writes interview reports into.
The estate's own front door under the name it was given first. It answered on the retired edge until now; christ.telno.services and this are the same board.

A phonebook name the retired edge answered with 502: the registry has always carried this host (see DIRECTORY_HOSTS in apps/telno/src/config.js), so the root goes to its page rather than a dead upstream.
The same phonebook under its other name, for the same reason: the registry carries it, the box that used to answer for it does not answer any more.
The directory's own name. It is in DIRECTORY_HOSTS, so it was always meant to answer here; until now its only vhost was on the retired edge.
